title: Why take a gap year
paragraphs: When you’ve finished your studies at school and college, do you feel like a well-earned rest? If you’re about to embark on a course at university, you’ll want to recharge your batteries, let your hair down and have some fun. But how long should you do that for? Now the idea of taking a year off before you move into further education seems to be the thing to do.

A year off – also called a gap year – is not a new concept, but there’s now a focus on making the most of this break from academic life. Long gone are the days of just hanging out on a beach or backpacking round the world. While that is still an option, a gap year is now more about gaining skills that will help you in later life. The BBC’s Smart Consumer podcast spoke to a student called Meg, who said “I just always had in the back of my mind I'd spend a year doing something productive and something that would just be good fun.”

Doing something productive is exactly what students are being encouraged to do because doing more purposeful things like work experience or charity work helps them acquire skills to use when competing for a place at university. It looks good on their CV and ultimately makes them more employable. Chris Rea is a Higher Education Services Manager from organisation, Prospects. He told the BBC that he thinks “the experience of the gap year has become actually much more practical, partly to do with university participation increasing, but also because of the demands on developing skills, specifically employability skills.”

While the benefits of taking a gap year are clear to see, some students worry they can’t afford it. Another student, Tom, told the BBC that to him, a gap year was an ‘alien concept’. He said “it would have been far too expensive and it's not something that I would have been able to rely on my parents or family members for.” But some experts say that it needn’t burn a hole in your pocket; you don’t need to travel far and you can even earn money by doing paid work.

For those who do have the funds, a combination of working, volunteering and travelling is undoubtedly an amazing opportunity. It increases confidence and independence, gives you a chance to learn new crafts, and gives you time to contemplate whether university is right for you.

vocabulary.entry: embark on /ɪmˈbɑːk ɒn/ 开始；开启（新的旅程、事业等）
vocabulary.example: She embarked on a new career in digital marketing.
vocabulary.translation: 她开启了数字营销领域的新职业生涯。

vocabulary.entry: recharge your batteries /ˌriːtʃɑːdʒ jɔː(r) ˈbætriz/ 养精蓄锐；恢复精力
vocabulary.example: I need a weekend away to recharge my batteries.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要外出度个周末来养精蓄锐。

vocabulary.entry: let your hair down /let jɔː(r) heə(r) daʊn/ 放松身心；不拘小节
vocabulary.example: We finally got to let our hair down at the company party.
vocabulary.translation: 我们终于能在公司派对上放松一下了。

vocabulary.entry: gap year /ɡæp jɪə(r)/ 间隔年（学业或工作之间的休学/休假年）
vocabulary.example: Many students take a gap year to travel or gain work experience.
vocabulary.translation: 很多学生利用间隔年旅行或获取工作经验。

vocabulary.entry: make the most of /meɪk ðə məʊst ɒv/ 充分利用
vocabulary.example: She made the most of her gap year by learning two languages.
vocabulary.translation: 她充分利用间隔年学会了两门语言。

vocabulary.entry: hang out /hæŋ aʊt/ 闲逛；逗留
vocabulary.example: We used to hang out at the mall after school.
vocabulary.translation: 我们以前放学后常去商场闲逛。

vocabulary.entry: backpacking /ˈbækpækɪŋ/ n. 背包旅行
vocabulary.example: He spent three months backpacking through Southeast Asia.
vocabulary.translation: 他花了三个月时间背包环游东南亚。

vocabulary.entry: productive /prəˈdʌktɪv/ adj. 有成效的；有意义的
vocabulary.example: It was a productive meeting that solved several key issues.
vocabulary.translation: 这是一次富有成效的会议，解决了多个关键问题。

vocabulary.entry: work experience /wɜːk ɪkˈspɪəriəns/ 工作实习；工作经验
vocabulary.example: Work experience in a law firm will boost your CV.
vocabulary.translation: 律师事务所的工作实习会让你的简历更有竞争力。

vocabulary.entry: charity work /ˈtʃærəti wɜːk/ 慈善工作；志愿服务
vocabulary.example: She dedicated her gap year to charity work in Africa.
vocabulary.translation: 她把间隔年用于非洲的慈善工作。

vocabulary.entry: acquire skills /əˈkwaɪə(r) skɪlz/ 习得技能；掌握技能
vocabulary.example: The course helps students acquire practical IT skills.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程帮助学生掌握实用的信息技术技能。

vocabulary.entry: compete for /kəmˈpiːt fɔː(r)/ 竞争；角逐
vocabulary.example: Hundreds of students compete for a place at the top university.
vocabulary.translation: 数百名学生竞争这所顶尖大学的入学名额。

vocabulary.entry: CV (Curriculum Vitae) /ˌsiː ˈviː/ 个人简历；履历
vocabulary.example: Make sure your CV highlights your relevant work experience.
vocabulary.translation: 确保你的简历突出展示相关的工作经验。

vocabulary.entry: employable /ɪmˈplɔɪəbl/ adj. 具备就业能力的；可雇用的
vocabulary.example: Graduates with internships are more employable than those without.
vocabulary.translation: 有实习经历的毕业生比没有的更具就业竞争力。

vocabulary.entry: Higher Education /ˌhaɪə(r) ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃn/ 高等教育
vocabulary.example: Higher education is crucial for career development in many fields.
vocabulary.translation: 高等教育对许多领域的职业发展至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: afford /əˈfɔːd/ v. 负担得起；有能力支付
vocabulary.example: We can't afford to go on a luxury holiday this year.
vocabulary.translation: 我们今年负担不起豪华度假的费用。

vocabulary.entry: alien concept /ˈeɪliən ˈkɒnsept/ 陌生的概念；难以理解的想法
vocabulary.example: Working from home was an alien concept to most people 20 years ago.
vocabulary.translation: 20年前，居家办公对大多数人来说是个陌生的概念。

vocabulary.term: burn a hole in your pocket
vocabulary.entry: burn a hole in your pocket /bɜːn ə həʊl ɪn jɔː(r) ˈpɒkɪt/ 花钱如流水；很快花光
vocabulary.example: That new smartphone will burn a hole in your pocket if you're not careful.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你不小心，那部新智能手机会让你花很多钱。

vocabulary.entry: funds /fʌndz/ n. 资金；钱款
vocabulary.example: The charity is seeking funds to build a new school.
vocabulary.translation: 该慈善机构正在筹集资金建造一所新学校。

vocabulary.entry: volunteering /ˌvɒlənˈtɪərɪŋ/ n. 志愿服务；义务工作
vocabulary.example: Volunteering at the animal shelter has been a rewarding experience.
vocabulary.translation: 在动物收容所做志愿服务是一次很有意义的经历。

vocabulary.entry: contemplate /ˈkɒntəmpleɪt/ v. 思考；考虑
vocabulary.example: She's contemplating whether to study abroad or stay in her home country.
vocabulary.translation: 她正在考虑是出国留学还是留在本国。

vocabulary.entry: craft /krɑːft/ n. 技能；手艺
vocabulary.example: He learned the craft of woodworking during his gap year.
vocabulary.translation: 他在间隔年期间学会了木工手艺。
